author: troy
content: interesting thing about SMS: for some status codes they reused codes from SM64

content: eg. `0xC400201`, also known as ACT_IDLE in SM64 makes a return

author: troy
content: `0xC000230` (ACT_JUMP_LAND_STOP) also exists here too

author: troy
content:
Turns out that they got lazy and just reused the action code system from SM64. It's pretty easy to decode statuses once you realize exactly how SM64 actions work. here's a few examples (hopefully i didnt make any mistakes)```
// NOTE: ACT_FLAG_RIDING_SHELL may have been repurposed for yoshi
0x00810446 (0x046 + ACT_FLAG_MOVING + ACT_FLAG_RIDING_SHELL + ACT_FLAG_ATTACKING)
0x0000133E (0x13E + ACT_FLAG_STATIONARY + ACT_FLAG_INTANGIBLE)
0x0C400201 (0x001 + ACT_FLAG_STATIONARY + ACT_FLAG_IDLE + ACT_FLAG_ALLOW_FIRST_PERSON + ACT_FLAG_PAUSE_EXIT)
0x00000383 (0x183 + ACT_FLAG_STATIONARY)
0x0000088C (0x08C + ACT_FLAG_AIR)
0x00000050 (0x050)
0x00020467 (0x067 + ACT_FLAG_MOVING + ACT_FLAG_INVULNERABLE)
0x0000088D (0x08D + ACT_FLAG_AIR)
0x00000891 (0x091 + ACT_FLAG_AIR)
0x0C000230 (0x030 + ACT_FLAG_STATIONARY)
0x00800447 (0x047 + ACT_FLAG_MOVING + ACT_FLAG_ATTACKING)
0x00001337 (0x137 + ACT_FLAG_STATIONARY + ACT_FLAG_INTANGIBLE)
0x000224E0 (0x0E0 + ACT_FLAG_MOVING + ACT_FLAG_SWIMMING + ACT_FLAG_INVULNERABLE)
0x000224E1 (0x0E1 + ACT_FLAG_MOVING + ACT_FLAG_SWIMMING + ACT_FLAG_INVULNERABLE)
0x00021313 (0x113 + ACT_FLAG_STATIONARY + ACT_FLAG_INTANGIBLE + ACT_FLAG_INVULNERABLE)
0x1000192A (0x12A + ACT_FLAG_AIR + ACT_FLAG_INTANGIBLE + ACT_FLAG_SWIMMING_OR_FLYING)
0x00000883 (0x083 + ACT_FLAG_AIR)
0x02000890 (0x090 + ACT_FLAG_AIR + ACT_FLAG_CONTROL_JUMP_HEIGHT)
0x000224E0 (0x0E0 + ACT_FLAG_MOVING + ACT_FLAG_SWIMMING + ACT_FLAG_INVULNERABLE)
```

author: Mrkol
content:
<@196019437172686849> quick lil review from just reading the code (at work rn so can't actually download it and check from inside the repo)
1) you forgot include guards on the header file
2) use the `/* 0xAD */ int unkAD;` style for unknown fields for consistency (and in the first place m_ was very unlikely to be used by C people for C structs, it's more of a C++ thing)
3) use snake_case for function args (or at least don't capitalize the first letter, we don't do that here)
4) `hx_wiper hx` and `unsigned int handle_type` -- global variables cannot be *defined* in headers because that would make their symbols leak into every single TU the header is included into, instead use the `extern` keyword to *declare* the variable without defining it and then define in the `.c` file
5) format the code with clang-format. easiest way to set it up is through vscode which downloads the binary automatically

author: Mrkol
content: when you see "incomplete type" errors that means that you need to add the include for this class into the cpp file

author: Mrkol
content: `class Foo;` <- this is a forward declaration. It declares the fact that the type exists, but does not specify it's size or contents, so it is considered to be incomplete

author: Mrkol
content: but even though it's incomplete, you can pass around pointers/references to it just fine, because for that it doesn't matter what the size or the contents are

author: Mrkol
content: the reason I use forward declarations everywhere is to avoid blowing up compilation times: each time you change a header all cpp files it is included into are recompiled. The more headers each other header includes, the worse it gets, exponentially

author: Mrkol
content: so whenever you can avoid pulling in additional includes into a header -- you should

author: Mrkol
content:
Now you decomp. The general process is:
1. select a TU you'd like to work on and make sure no one else is working on it
2. filter out all symbols from the mario.MAP file that are located in that TU, demangle and make them into respective functions/variables/etc
3. create headers required for the TU to compile: function declarations, class/struct definitions, etc
4. start analyzing the relevant classes/structs in ghidra, filling in their fields, figuring out which methods are static, etc
5. start filling out the fields in the code. in the process you might discover that you need additional headers from other TUs, in which case tackle those
6. start roughly decompiling a function in the TU by referencing ghidra's automatic decompilation. m2c or ida can sometimes be useful too
7. match the roughly decompiled function by looking at the asm in objdiff
8. goto 6 until no functions are left in the TU
9. goto 1 until all of sms is decompiled
Note however that at any one of those steps you might get a bit stuck and not complete it 100% from the get-go. It's ok to get it 80% of the way there and skip to the next step. It is also OK to submit PRs with 80% done TUs, any progress is good progress
